reachable: Yes, at the scored read position and with gradient in training. (1) Layout: L = 2*maxn and the coded command sits at even indices, so the cups instrument's read position (2*r, cmd valid, obs absent) carries a coded token. (2) The coding is applied to the read command too — its SRC slot is the read path, DST slot the NULL code. (3) The arch's transport read s_i = a_src_i^T mem is computed at EVERY command position regardless of whether that step's observation is present; only the WRITE is gated by obs_live = valid_obs & valid_cmd, and the write happens after the read, so the missing observation at the read position does not switch the mechanism off (this is the failure mode that has been fatal before — it is not present here). All move steps in a scored window have observations present, so they do write. (4) Empirically, on a scoring-shaped window (5 steps, L=9, obs withheld at the read) after 8 real training steps of the full genome: rerouting a move while keeping the read command byte-identical changes the prediction at the read by max|Δ| 0.055, and flipping only the read command's SRC-code coordinates changes it by 0.505. (5) Gradient reaches the mechanism: after 6 steps of the real _train closure, |grad| is 0.43 on addr_in.weight, 0.070 on addr_src.weight, 0.074 on addr_dst.weight, 26.8 on tp_out.weight. The transport channel's own contribution at the read is small this early (0.002) purely because tp_out is zero-init, which is by design.
solves_outside_model: No. parse_command and _command_code are pure functions of ONE command string — they never touch another step, an observation, a target, or any already-applied move. The code is a re-tokenization (a lexical hash of source path, destination path, and six verb/shape flags), not a resolution. Verified three ways: prefix-causality holds exactly (coding cmds[:k+1] equals the first k+1 rows of coding the whole sequence, for every k in a real sequence); the read-position token is bit-identical between a native chain and a role-swapped chain over the same board while the move tokens differ; and no observation or target tensor is read anywhere on the coding path (collate uses z_obs only for the obs tokens and tgt, exactly as the baseline does). This is the legitimate kind of command parsing — it shapes the INPUT ENCODING of each command in isolation, it does not hand the model the resolved routing. It is nothing like the retracted stream, which stamped the resolved identity into the read token.
summary:
The code does what the hypothesis says. Every structural and numeric claim I could execute checks out.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION: 208 coordinates in three disjoint hash-chosen index sets (96/96/16, union 208, pairwise disjoint, deterministic from blake2b of the coordinate number). The claimed command-shape census of evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl reproduces EXACTLY — (W,P) 401, (W,P,P) 172, (W,P,R,P) 81, (W,W,P) 59, (W,) 7, (W,W) 4 — and the parser gets every shape right (cat A >> B → src A dst B; mv A B → src A dst B; ls -1 / → src / no dst; bare ls → NULL/NULL). Against the baseline collate on the same batch: types, key_pad, tgt, cmd_mask bit-identical; observation tokens bit-identical; padded command rows bit-identical; exactly the 208 slot coordinates differ on valid command rows, all values ±1, and the other 560 are bit-identical. Prefix-causal at every cut. Read token identical under a role-swapped chain, move tokens different. Path-code inner products: identical path 1.000, the cited .cfg.7 / .cfg.8 pair -0.0208 (claimed -0.021), off-diagonal std 0.102 over the 293 real paths (claimed 0.10). Timings reproduce (5.08 / 8.68 / 19.75 ms vs claimed ~5.5 / ~8.4 / ~19). The module imports only hashlib and torch. Genome bookkeeping is accurate: arch and objective from the partner, batcher from the parent with params verbatim, optim/target/head identical in both parents. The claim that r3 is the only one of the two objectives that opts into ctx is correct (r12 has no WANTS_CTX). The full genome trains end to end on CPU without NaN.

I also checked the one argument the author explicitly flagged as UNMEASURED — that the pooled command embedding is the bottleneck — using the real embedding cache they had no access to, and it is true and stronger than they claimed. In standardized space: mv commands differing only in trailing path suffixes have cosine 0.983 (min 0.917, n=2751); mv A B vs mv B A has cosine 0.996 (n=471); random mv/mv pairs 0.233. So both stated facts — near-parallel distinct addresses and near-symmetry in the two arguments — hold on the actual data.

Three minor divergences, none affecting what gets scored: the out-of-fold claim about the ridge is wrong (and wrong in the direction of MORE suppression of the location-keyed shortcut, i.e. against the author's own risk 4, not toward inflating the score); the timing figures are labelled "measured" though the jail has no torch, while the values themselves are right; and the SRC/DST equality is exact in the code but requires the two address heads to learn a shared alignment, which the write-up slightly under-states.

ONE CAVEAT FOR READING THE NUMBER, not a divergence. This coding makes exact path matching free, and that lowers the cost of the position-keyed lookup family the analytic band covers — e.g. "copy the observation of the exposure step whose command path equals the FIRST move's source", which the r23 pointer-softmax can express directly and which does not cancel in the paired difference. The author names the location-keyed version of this (risk 4, which does cancel) but not the move-order-keyed version. Read the score against the band reported beside it and against the swapped-held diagnostic.

COULD NOT CHECK: anything about the actual score or training dynamics at the real step budget (whether the address heads converge on the alignment, whether the delta-rule memory saturates, whether destroying 208 coordinates degrades the non-routed cat/ls retrieval, and whether 64-d projections of 96-bit codes collide inside a real window). Also unchecked: the side effect on the head, whose same-path triple mining thresholds cosine on the now-coded command tokens at 0.60 — the coding pushes different-path pairs down and same-path pairs up, which changes which triples get mined. That interaction is not claimed either way in the hypothesis.

divergences.claim: "the hash codes do not generalize out of fold, so the ridge can still only remove what genuinely generalizes" — used to argue the r3 cross-fit nuisance ridge cannot over-subtract once the address code is in its basis.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The code is a deterministic function of the path string, so the SAME 96-dim ±1 pattern recurs on every row that mentions that path. r3's _crossfit_nuisance splits rows by flattened-row PARITY, and a path recurs across steps inside a single sequence, so identical code blocks land in both folds and the ridge can exploit them out of fold. In all 24 sampled training sequences some path appears at both an even and an odd step index (24/24), and every sequence has at least one repeated path.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/objective/r3_fwl_orthogonalized_ring_contrast.py:66-86 (parity fold, basis = ctx["cmd"] = coded command tokens via harness.py:_train ctx construction); counted over evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl: 24/24 sequences contain a path occurring at both even and odd step indices.

divergences.claim: "measured on the sample trajectories (CPU, 64-sequence batches), collate with the coding takes ~5.5 ms per batch warm and ~8.4 ms with the hash cache cleared every batch, against ~19 ms for the baseline collate" — stated as a measurement.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The numbers are correct — I reproduce 5.08 ms warm, 8.68 ms cold-cache, 19.75 ms baseline on 64-sequence CPU batches built from the sample file. But the measurement requires torch, which the inventor jail does not have, so the provenance word "measured" is not supportable even though the values are right.
divergences.evidence: Timed impl.collate vs realenv.seq_worldmodel.collate over 64 sequences drawn from evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl, 20 reps each, CPU.

divergences.claim: "the DEST slot of a move and the SOURCE slot of a later command have normalized inner product 1.0 when the paths are equal ... The code makes both operations exact and linear."
divergences.what_the_code_does: As 96-vectors the inner product is exactly 1.0 (verified), but SRC and DST occupy DISJOINT coordinate sets (_SRC_IDX / _DST_IDX), so no single linear functional of the token computes that equality. The arch must learn addr_dst applied to the DST coordinates and addr_src applied to the SRC coordinates to agree as functions of the same path — two independent 256→64 matrices after a shared LayerNorm+GELU. The equality is exact in the CODE; it is a learning problem in the MODEL. The author's failure mode 3 covers the recovery loss but not the head-alignment requirement explicitly.
divergences.evidence: impl _SRC_IDX/_DST_IDX disjoint (verified: 96/96/16, union 208, pairwise disjoint); evolve/chunks/arch/r23_dual_address_transport_pointer.py:47-51 (addr_ln → addr_in(768→256) → gelu → addr_src/addr_dst, two separate (64,256) matrices).
